This is claim petition u/s 166/140 of M.V. Act seeking compensation for petitioners in respect of death of late Ram Chander Sharma s/o late Hare Ram Sharma in a road side accident.
As per the averments on 24.04.2022 deceased Ram Chander Sharma was traveling by the bike bearing registration no.DL-5SAR-9277 from Shahdara to Jawahar Nagar, Ghaziabd.

When deceased reached near street no.10, Gulab Vatika, offending vehicle/car no.UP-16DB-2914 which was being driven by respondent no.1 at very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit the deceased on his motorcycle from behind.
Due to forceful impact deceased sustained fatal injuries.
After the accident he was taken to GTB Hospital where he was declared 'brought dead'.
Post mortem was conducted in that hospital.

2. It is mentioned in the claim petition that deceased at the time of accident was 42 years of age and was working as confectioner (halwai) MACT No.298/2022 by SHELENDER SHELENDER MALIK Page 2 MALIK Date: 2024.10.03 17:24:50 +0530 in Ghaziabad and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
It is stated that petitioners have been left behind, (petitioner no.1 and three minor children being petitioner no.2 to 4).
it is stated that accident occurred due rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1, respondent no.2 and 3 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle respectively.
3. After filing of the claim petition respondent no.1 and 2 after service put appearance and filed the WS, wherein it is pleaded that allegations made in the claim petition are not correct.
It is stated that no such accident as alleged has taken place.
Respondents denied the liability and the manner in which accident alleged to have taken place.
4. Respondent no.3/insurance filed the legal offer for sum of Rs.10,97,756/-.

Perusal of the record shows that matter could not be settled despite efforts and therefore on 07.12.2023 this Tribunal proceeded to frame following issues :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no.UP-5SAR-9277 (should be UP-16DB-2914) on 24.04.2022 at about 11:00 pm nearby Gali no.10,
Gulab Vatika within the jurisdiction of PS Loni Border, Distt.
Ghaziabad, U.P. in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh.Ram Chander Sharma?

It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

Thus, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no.UP- 16DB-2914 being driven by respondent no.1.
Issue No.2 10.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result MACT No.298/2022

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 11.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Ram Chander Sharma.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There MACT No.298/2022 SHELENDER by SHELENDER Page 6 MALIK Date: 2024.10.03 17:25:14 +0530 will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

sentences.text: Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased 13.
Petitioner no.1 Devki (PW1) in her evidence has deposed that her husband Ram Chandra Sharma was 42 years of age at the time of accident.
PW1 has proved PAN card, Aadhar card, election ID card and driving licence of deceased as Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/4.
In the driving licence of the deceased his date of birth is mentioned to be 04.12.1979.
There is no dispute to these documents including date of birth of the deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (24.04.2022) was 42 years.
Assessment of Income of deceased 14.

Petitioner no.1 (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased husband was working as a confectioner (halwai) on contractual basis as a freelancer in Delhi and in addition to providing service to Shri Ram Sweets and Bakers and was earning Rs.25,000/- to Rs.30,000/- per month.

However during cross examination PW1 stated that her husband was earning about Rs.20,000/- per month as he used to work for Mr.Parveen as well as his own work and he used to received salary of Rs.20,000/- in cash from his employer Parveen.
Witness says that beside bank account details of her husband she does not have any documentary proof to prove the said salary of her husband.

Though PW1 claimed in her MACT No.298/2022 SHELENDER MALIK Date: 2024.10.03 17:25:26 +0530 evidence that her deceased husband used to earn Rs.25,000/- to Rs.30,000/- per month by working as confectioner/halwai as well as doing freelance work, however there is no documentary proof with regard to such deposition.
Even no employer by the name of Parveen has been examined by the petitioners to prove the fact that deceased was working with him.
Even otherwise in the written submissions, petitioners have made assessment of income of deceased on the basis of minimum wages.

In the absence of any such evidence, this Tribunal assesses income of the deceased at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi which at the time of accident was of Rs.16,506/- per month.
Application of Multiplier 15.
As held above, deceased was 42 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:

sentences.text: In view of the above, multiplier of 14 has to be applied against the age bracket of 41 to 45 years to determine the compensation.
Future Prospects 17.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

18. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 42 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (aged between 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
8.
Thus, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no.UP- 16DB-2914 being driven by respondent no.1.
Issue No.2 10.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result MACT No.298/2022
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
In the absence of any such evidence, this Tribunal assesses income of the deceased at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi which at the time of accident was of Rs.16,506/- per month.
Application of Multiplier 15.
As held above, deceased was 42 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
